notes: Fixes the regression and tests it thoroughly, but it hardcodes reverse-proxy placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher and also treats the upstream.duration placeholders as response data, which the spec did not ask for.

Works and passes, but it puts reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp MatchExpression, and it adds upstream.duration placeholders beyond the agreed list (they aren't set at retry-evaluation time); some retry e2e cases, like status_codes == "", don't discriminate pre- from post-fix.

Correct, and slightly more precise than the reference because it folds constant string concatenations into static names; that extra folding logic, the linter-appeasing switch and the added integration test make it heavier than needed.
Correct, with very thorough unit, e2e and integration tests; it adds constant-folding of concatenated placeholder names and a small interface, which go beyond what was needed but are sound.

Uses the same AST-based design as the reference, with a careful ph-call detection and a generic PlaceholderNames API; its end-to-end tests cover the request-only, lookalike, escaped, upstream.host, ph(), status_text, dynamic-name and latency cases.

Matches the reference: it collects static placeholder names and a dynamic flag from the checked AST, then classifies them in reverseproxy; tests are broad, though the latency e2e test depends on timing and the doc edit drops the is_transport_error mention.

Closely mirrors the reference: it collects statically known placeholder names from the checked CEL AST, flags non-literal names as dynamic, and adds a response-placeholder predicate in reverseproxy, with focused unit and end-to-end tests covering every spec case.

Closest to the reference: it reuses the existing isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall and isCELStringLiteral helpers, treats non-literal names as dynamic, and keeps the classification in reverseproxy, with focused unit tests (including mixed matcher sets) and e2e tests.

Closely follows the reference in both backends, stores the links flag at New, and lets a regular `x.rclonelink` member win over a symlink `x`; it adds docs and thorough tests, including hostile-copy tests for zip and squashfs, at the cost of some extra complexity.

Correctly suffixes symlinks in both backends, captures --links at New time, and keeps List and NewObject in agreement; it also handles a regular member colliding with a translated link name, though the deferred-link logic in readZip is a little convoluted.

The zip side works and adds a defensive filter for members under a symlink, but squashfs reads --links from each List/NewObject ctx instead of storing it at New. That breaks when the Fs is built with --links and listed with another ctx, which probably explains the failed hidden test; an offset past the target length also makes Open error instead of clamping.

Squashfs reads the links setting from each call's ctx instead of the Fs (inconsistent with zip), the zip backend hides members under a symlink even without --links (an unrequested behaviour change), Open fails when offset exceeds the target length, and it fails one hidden test.

Squashfs mirrors the reference via StatT.LinkTarget and tests are good, but zip only adds the suffix when the name doesn't already end in .rclonelink. A symlink named `foo.rclonelink` is therefore exposed unsuffixed and recreated as symlink `foo`, which is also inconsistent with the squashfs side.

Works for the main cases and has good tests, but in zip it skips the .rclonelink suffix for any symlink whose name already ends in it (mangling the name and diverging from squashfs), and in squashfs it silently uses an empty target when stat info is missing.

A sound implementation that stores links at New, always suffixes listed symlinks, and makes NewObject and List agree; it has strong unit and archive-level copy tests. Weak points are lenient root-name handling with a small inconsistency in the single-object suffix case, and a readlink comment that contradicts the code.

Solid implementation with consistent suffixing (including symlinks already ending in .rclonelink), offset clamping, and good tests including copy and hostile-escape tests; root handling accepts both name forms and is somewhat convoluted, and a regular member colliding with a link name is not handled.
